items.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: it was Johann Strauss’ birthday or death, or something “So we want you to go to the statue and play the national anthem.”

ctx.x: So of course Eric went in ’64 but then Jimmy.

Jimmy came here. He called up Keiko and asked, this is just before he died, he said, “I need $150.” So she wrote a check and we said we’d leave it with the doorman. So he says, “Okay.” I know the check was gone and I didn’t see Jimmy again. Somebody picked it up. That’s strange because his wife, Roberta, her father was one of the wealthiest doctors in San Francisco, I mean rich! She had stocks, and bonds, and all kinds of stuff. (Laughs) And she had him put in jail for child support! That’s mean, that’s cruel.…
So that was a very special group for you then.
